chunks: Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyya. He said:

The Master of Worshippers, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), looked at Ubaydullah ibn al-Abbas ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and shed tears. Then he said: There is not a day more severe for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) than the day of Uhud, in which his uncle Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Lion of God and the Lion of His Messenger, was killed. After it, the day of Mu'ta, in which his cousin Ja'far ibn Abi Talib was killed.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: But there is no day like the day of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Thirty thousand men advanced upon him, claiming to be from this community, each seeking nearness to God, Mighty and Majestic, through his blood. He was reminding them by God, yet they did not heed, until they killed him treacherously, oppressively, and antagonistically.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: May God have mercy on al-Abbas, for indeed he sacrificed and endured hardship, and redeemed his brother with his own soul until his two hands were severed. So God, Mighty and Majestic, compensated him with two wings with which he flies with the angels in Paradise, just as He gave to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. And surely al-Abbas has a station with God, Blessed and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection that all the martyrs will envy.

key_terms.آثر: Showed altruistic preference/self-sacrifice (ithar) — a Quranic virtue
key_terms.أسد الله: Lion of God, title of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle
key_terms.ازدلف: Came down upon/advanced against — implies an overwhelming multitude rushing to attack
key_terms.سيد العابدين: Master of the Worshippers, a title of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (AS)
key_terms.يتقرب إلى الله: Seeking closeness to God (taqarrub), here used with bitter irony as the killers falsely believed they were performing an act of worship

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about al-Abbas ibn Ali and the day of Karbala?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (AS) — the fourth Imam who himself survived the tragedy of Karbala — recounts a hierarchy of the most painful days for the Prophet, placing the day of Karbala as uniquely devastating: those who killed al-Husayn (AS) were not enemies but people claiming to be Muslims seeking God's favor. The narration then eulogizes al-Abbas ibn Ali, the half-brother and standard-bearer of al-Husayn at Karbala, whose arms were cut off and who is described as being given divine wings to fly with the angels, a rank that even all the martyrs will envy on Judgment Day.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
